segments.t: Back at the ASK offices, tensions run high following Hicham's arrival as majority owner. While Gabriel checks in on his colleagues, an exhausted Mathias snaps at callers over Ramzy's departure. Worried about Mathias's health, Noémie proposes an unusual alternative cure. Let's listen to the scene in French first.
Ça va? Vous avez mangé?
Oui, un soda zéro sucre.
Je suis juste venu proposer mon aide.
Agence ASK, bonjour? Je ne représente plus Ramzy!
Je n'ai pas le numéro de son agent!
Où va ce pays?
Mathias, vous avez vu un médecin?
Je n'ai pas le temps de dormir ou courir.
Des évanouissements, ça peut être grave! Vous auriez pu vous tuer!
Vous connaissez le chamanisme?
Pas vraiment. Pourquoi?
Je sais que vous êtes sceptique, mais je connais un chaman extraordinaire.
Je pourrais vous mettre en contact avec lui...
Let's examine how Noémie tries to help Mathias step by step.
Ça va? Vous avez mangé?
'How are you? Have you eaten?' Gabriel politely inquires. He uses a common everyday phrase to ask how things are going, followed by the formal 'you'. This is perfectly natural in French.
Oui, un soda zéro sucre.
'Yes, a zero-sugar soda.' Noémie answers about her lunch. The term for soda is a direct borrowing, paired with a descriptor for zero. In French, it works nicely.
Je suis juste venu proposer mon aide.
'I just came to offer my help.' Gabriel explains his presence. The concept of help is joined by a possessive piece meaning 'my'. The French use this a lot.
Agence ASK, bonjour? Je ne représente plus Ramzy!

'ASK agency, hello? I no longer represent Ramzy!' Mathias barks into his phone. He uses a negative structure meaning 'no longer' or 'not anymore' around the core action for representing. In French, it sounds perfect.
Je n'ai pas le numéro de son agent!
'I do not have her agent's phone number!' Mathias vents his frustration. The term for a number is used here to mean a phone number specifically. This is standard in French.
Où va ce pays?
'What is this country coming to?' Mathias expresses exasperation. He asks literally 'where goes this country' using a simple question piece for 'where'. A nice sentence in French.
Mathias, vous avez vu un médecin?
'Mathias, have you seen a doctor?' Noémie voices genuine concern. The term for a doctor is used with a common action meaning to see, in a past tense structure. A great expression in French.
Je n'ai pas le temps de dormir ou courir.
'I do not have time to sleep or run.' Mathias dismisses medical advice. A handy chunk for 'I do not have the time' is followed by a core action for sleeping. You can say this in French.
Des évanouissements, ça peut être grave! Vous auriez pu vous tuer!
'Fainting spells can be serious! You could have killed yourself!' Noémie warns him. The term for serious can also mean grave or heavy in other contexts. In French, this is widely used.
Vous connaissez le chamanisme?
'Do you know about shamanism?' Noémie introduces a new topic. She uses a core meaning to know or be familiar with something. The French love this expression.
Pas vraiment. Pourquoi?
'Not really. Why?' Mathias responds with polite detachment. A short, handy expression for 'not really' uses a piece that means truly or really. In French, it fits perfectly.
Je sais que vous êtes sceptique, mais je connais un chaman extraordinaire.
'I know you are skeptical, but I know an extraordinary shaman.' Noémie anticipates his doubts. She uses a clear cognate for skeptical and another for extraordinary. A nice way to say it in French.
Je pourrais vous mettre en contact avec lui...

'I could put you in touch with him...' Noémie makes her offer. A handy expression for connecting two people translates literally as 'put in contact'. In French, it is a great choice. Now let's listen to the scene once more from beginning to end.
Ça va? Vous avez mangé?
Oui, un soda zéro sucre.
Je suis juste venu proposer mon aide.
Agence ASK, bonjour? Je ne représente plus Ramzy!
Je n'ai pas le numéro de son agent!
Où va ce pays?
Mathias, vous avez vu un médecin?
Je n'ai pas le temps de dormir ou courir.
Des évanouissements, ça peut être grave! Vous auriez pu vous tuer!
Vous connaissez le chamanisme?
Pas vraiment. Pourquoi?
Je sais que vous êtes sceptique, mais je connais un chaman extraordinaire.
Je pourrais vous mettre en contact avec lui...
Noémie is eager to help Mathias recover from his fainting spell by introducing him to her spiritual healer. See you next time!
Bonne journée!
